newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly to probe LILCO-Brooklyn Union deal.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly to probe LILCO-Brooklyn Union deal.

text.p: The New York State Assembly Thursday said it will hold a series of hearings to probe if a deal for the Long Island Power Authority to buy assets from Long Island Lighting Co will "truly" cut rates.
The Authority last month reached a pact to buy assets from Long Island Lighting Co and Brooklyn Union Gas.

In a prepared release, Silver said: "Our top priority is relief from high energy costs for all New Yorkers. Long Island ratepayers, for example, have struggled for years to pay the highest electric bills in the nation."

New York State Gov George Pataki has said the agreement eventually would cut Long Island's electricity rates by 20 percent over the next five years. The deal, which requires a host of state and federal regulators to approve it, would be financed by the sale of up to $7.26 billion of tax-exempt bonds--the largest such transaction in history.

The hearings were announced jointly by Silver and Assemblyman Energy Committee Chairman Paul Tonko, D-Amsterdam. The release said: "He and Assemblyman Tonko said the hearing will investigate whether the proposed Long Island Power Authority takeover of certain LILCO functions and assets will truly provide the significant, real, long-term relief that is promised for it."
The first hearing will be held on April 17 at the Western Campus of Suffolk Community College.
